newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty closes flat after dip, seen poised for gains.
newsitem.headline: Zloty closes flat after dip, seen poised for gains.

text.p: The Polish zloty stabilized at last week's closing levels at around one percent weaker than the trading band centre after an early fall triggered by one exporter order, dealers said.
"The zloty returned to its two-week-old range between parity and minus 1.5 percent," said Jaroslaw Dryjski, forex dealer at Bank Slaski SA.

Dealers expected the central bank to intervene if the zloty eased below 1.5 percent from parity and said that being at the lower end of the band poised the local unit for gains, rather than losses, in the near-term.

Dealers said the market would either remain shallow and sleepy until the September 21 parliamentary elections, or could see some speculative foreign inflows just before the polls from players taking advantage of the zloty's volatility.

The zloty closed at 1.04/1.13 percent weaker than the trading band centre against Thursday's close at minus 1.06/1.13 below parity. It closed at at 3.4700/30 to the dollar, against 3.4870/00 on Thursday and at 1.9060/80 to the mark, against 1.8995/05.
At Monday's primary T-bill auction all minimal prices fell on demand of 911 million zlotys against a 1.1 billion offer.
Dealers said the finance ministry may further lower the prices to attract more buyers next week. Foreign investors were virtually absent at today's auction.
Dealers expected one-day rates to rise slightly following the rise in T-bill yields. The maximum 52-week T-bill yield rose to 23.0 percent at the tender and the average was 22.97 percent.
Overnight rates closed at 21.00/23.00 percent against Thursday's 22.45/23.00 percent. Tomorrow/next were at 21.50/21.95 percent against 22.90/23.30 percent on Thursday.
